result.title: Climbing the Design Ladder: Sequential Knowledge Distillation for Early-Stage Circuit Timing Prediction
result.summary: Integrated circuit design involves multiple design stages: logic synthesis, floorplanning, placement, and routing, with each stage taking hours to weeks to complete. Discovering timing violations late in this flow forces costly iterations back to earlier stages, wasting computational resources and delaying product launches. While predicting post-routing timing from early-stage data could prevent these failures, existing machine learning approaches struggle with the massive abstraction gap between post-synthesis logical descriptions and post-routing physical layouts. We propose STEP-KD (Sequential Timing Evaluation via Progressive Knowledge Distillation), which leverages intermediate design stages as ``stepping stones'' for progressive knowledge transfer rather than attempting direct prediction. STEP-KD trains teacher models at the post-routing, post-placement, and post-floorplan stages, then sequentially distills their knowledge to a post-synthesis student model through representation alignment. Experiments on diverse circuits demonstrate that STEP-KD reduces timing prediction error compared to direct distillation and supervised baselines, and in most settings compared to the industry-standard Static Timing Analysis (STA) tool. STEP-KD reduces the weighted mean absolute percentage error of Total Negative Slack prediction to 19.78\%, compared with 74.84\% for STA. Our proposed method is step forward to identify timing problems earlier, avoiding expensive late-stage redesigns.

AI.brief_summary: 该论文针对集成电路早期阶段的时序预测问题，提出 STEP-KD：不再从综合后描述直接预测布线后时序，而是把 floorplan、placement、routing 等中间设计阶段当作「踏脚石」，用多阶段教师模型逐级向综合后学生模型做表征对齐式知识蒸馏。
AI.relevance_reason: 「阶段递进 + 表征对齐蒸馏」与 LVR 中跨抽象层级的潜在状态传递、逐级监督与贡献分配可能有概念联系，可供核查其渐进蒸馏是否类似视觉细节在中间状态中的保留与坍缩问题；但领域为电路时序，需较多迁移判断。
